tagline: Pure holding company controlling 50.005% of Heineken N.V., providing strategic oversight and stability to the HEINEKEN group without direct operational activities
hero_kpi_rationale: Heineken Holding N.V. holds exactly 50.005% of the shares in Heineken N.V., ensuring decisive control over the HEINEKEN group despite the absence of direct operational activities. This unique stake defines the group's governance structure.
company_description: Heineken N.V. brews and sells beer and cider in Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East, and the Asia Pacific. The company also provides soft drinks. It sells its products under the Heineken, Heineken 0.0, Heineken Silver, Amstel, Moretti, Tiger, Desperados, Edelweiss, Lagunitas, Orchard Thieves, Windhoek, Dos Equis, Red Stripe, Kingfisher, Bintang, Gosser, Affligem, Mort Subite, Strongbow, Stassen, Bulmers, Old Mout, Savanna, Turbo King, Tecate, Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher, Bia Viet, Tiger Crystal, Birra Moretti, Harar, Cruzcampo, Bernini, Legend Stout, Beavertown, Stëlz, Texels, Ladrón, Bandida, Stibitzer, El Aguila, and Murphy's brands. In addition, the company engages in rental of pubs and bars; wholesale activities; and pub management and technical services. The company offers its products to retailers, wholesalers and distributors, bars, restaurants, clubs, cafes, and hotels. Heineken N.V. was incorporated in 1864 and is headquartered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. Heineken N.V. is a subsidiary of Heineken Holding N.V.

risks.title: Structural dependency on Heineken N.V.
risks.summary: Heineken Holding N.V. is a pure holding company with no direct operational activities. It relies entirely on dividends paid by Heineken N.V. to remunerate its shareholders. Any reduction or suspension of dividends from Heineken N.V. would directly impact the holding's distribution capacity.
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk mentioned upfront: Heineken Holding N.V. has no operational activities, only distributes dividends received from Heineken N.V., and employs no staff. Central in Item 1A, explicit language on total dependency, stable but structural trend, critical weight for the holding's viability.

risks.title: Absence of internal risk management system
risks.summary: Unlike Heineken N.V., Heineken Holding N.V. has not implemented an internal risk management and control system. This absence is justified by the lack of operational activities, but creates vulnerability in case of crisis or structural change.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly stated: « Heineken Holding N.V., unlike Heineken N.V., does not have an internal risk management and control system ». Mentioned twice in Item 1A, direct and unambiguous language, stable trend by structural design, high weight for governance.

risks.title: Shareholder concentration and control risk
risks.summary: A single shareholder (Mrs C.L. de Carvalho-Heineken) controls over 52% of the capital via L'Arche Holding S.A. This extreme concentration limits the power of other shareholders (FEMSA 14.94%, Gardner Russo 3.78%, Harris Associates 3.05%) and creates a risk of unilateral decisions.
risks.score_rationale: Mrs C.L. de Carvalho-Heineken holds 52.01% of the capital (including L'Arche Holding S.A. at 50.005%), creating extreme concentration. Explicitly mentioned with precise data, neutral language but revealing figures, stable trend since 2006, major weight for governance and minority rights.

risks.title: Voting restrictions and limited shareholder rights
risks.summary: A contractual agreement imposes voting restrictions on a specific shareholder if its holdings exceed certain thresholds (20% of capital or 20% economic interest in Heineken N.V.). These restrictions limit transparency and voting fluidity.
risks.score_rationale: Voting rights restriction applies to a specific shareholder if holdings exceed 20% of capital or 20% economic interest in Heineken N.V. Mentioned in section « Restrictions related to shares », technical language but significant impact, stable trend, moderate weight for minority shareholders.

risks.title: Single-tier governance with partial non-compliance
risks.summary: Heineken Holding N.V. applies a single-tier governance structure (one-tier board) since 2012, with 2 executive and 4 non-executive members. However, it does not formally comply with Dutch Corporate Governance Code best-practice provisions III.8.1 and III.8.4, as former executive members cannot serve as chairman or be considered independent.
risks.score_rationale: One-tier structure implemented in 2012 with formal non-application of best-practice provisions III.8.1 and III.8.4 of the Code. Justification: former executive members cannot be chairman or independent. Explicitly mentioned with Code references, technical language but reveals intentional deviation, stable trend since 2012, moderate weight for compliance.

risks.title: Control change risk and required approvals
risks.summary: Any material change in the nature or identity of Heineken Holding N.V. (business transfer, entry/exit from long-term cooperations, acquisition/disposal of substantial interests) requires joint approval from the meeting of priority shareholders and the General Meeting, which may slow down strategic decisions.
risks.score_rationale: Any material change in the nature or identity of the company requires approval from the meeting of priority shareholders AND the General Meeting. Mentioned in section « Board of Directors' resolutions », explicit language with enumeration of cases (business transfer, long-term cooperations, acquisitions), stable trend, moderate weight for major transactions.

risks.title: Dependency on priority shareholders for governance
risks.summary: The 250 priority shares, held by two foundations, grant the right to propose a non-binding list of candidates for each Board of Directors appointment. Although non-binding, this list influences General Meeting decisions and represents a historical governance mechanism.
risks.score_rationale: The 250 priority shares (0.01% of capital) held by two foundations (Stichting Administratiekantoor Priores and Stichting Beheer Prioriteitsaandelen) have the right to propose a non-binding list of candidates for each Board appointment. Mentioned in section « Priority shares », technical language, stable trend since inception, low but symbolic weight for governance.
